**Josep Borrell Fontelles**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-1) (born 24 April 1947) is a Spanish politician who served as [High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Representative_of_the_Union_for_Foreign_Affairs_and_Security_Policy "High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy") and [Vice-President of the European Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice-President_of_the_European_Commission "Vice-President of the European Commission") from 2019 to 2024. A member of the [Spanish Socialist Workers' Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Socialist_Workers'_Party "Spanish Socialist Workers' Party") (PSOE), he served as [President of the European Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_European_Parliament "President of the European Parliament") from 2004 to 2007 and as Spain's [Minister of Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_Foreign_Affairs_(Spain) "Minister of Foreign Affairs (Spain)") from 2018 to 2019.

Born and raised in the Catalan village of [La Pobla de Segur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Pobla_de_Segur "La Pobla de Segur"), Borrell is an aeronautical engineer and economist by training as well as a professor of mathematics. He entered politics in the 1970s as a member of the PSOE during [Spain's transition to democracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_transition_to_democracy "Spanish transition to democracy"), and went on to serve in several positions during the governments of [Felipe González](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felipe_Gonz%C3%A1lez "Felipe González"), first within the Ministry of Economy and Finance as General Secretary for the Budget and Public Spending (1982–1984) and [Secretary of State for Finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_State_for_Finance "Secretary of State for Finance") (1984–1991), then joining the [Council of Ministers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_Ministers_(Spain) "Council of Ministers (Spain)") as [Minister of Public Works and Transport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Development_(Spain) "Ministry of Development (Spain)") (1991–1996). In the opposition after the 1996 election, Borrell unexpectedly won the PSOE primary in 1998 and became [Leader of the Opposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leader_of_the_Opposition_(Spain) "Leader of the Opposition (Spain)") and the designated prime ministerial candidate of the party until he resigned in 1999. He then switched to European politics, becoming a [Member of the European Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_the_European_Parliament "Member of the European Parliament") (MEP) during the 2004–2009 legislative period and serving as [President of the European Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_European_Parliament "President of the European Parliament") for the first half of the term.

He returned to the [Council of Ministers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_Ministers_(Spain) "Council of Ministers (Spain)") in June 2018, when he was appointed [Minister of Foreign Affairs, the European Union and Cooperation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Foreign_Affairs_(Spain) "Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Spain)") in the [Sánchez government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A1nchez_I_Government "Sánchez I Government"). In July 2019, Borrell was announced as the [European Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Council "European Council")'s nominee to be appointed [High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Representative_of_the_Union_for_Foreign_Affairs_and_Security_Policy "High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy"). He took office in December 2019.

## Early life and career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Josep_Borrell&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and career")]

Josep (or José)[[n. 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-2) Borrell Fontelles was born on 24 April 1947 in the Catalan village of [La Pobla de Segur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Pobla_de_Segur "La Pobla de Segur"), [province of Lleida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Province_of_Lleida "Province of Lleida"), near the [Pyrenees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrenees "Pyrenees"), son of Joan Borrell (father) and Luisa Fontelles Doll (mother).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-pobladesegur-3)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-4) He grew up in the village, where his father owned a small bakery.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-auto-5)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:1-6)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:3-7) His paternal grandparents were Spanish immigrants in [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina "Argentina"), where they ran a bakery in the city of [Mendoza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mendoza,_Argentina "Mendoza, Argentina"), close to the [General San Martín Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_San_Mart%C3%ADn_Park "General San Martín Park").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:3-7)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-8) They returned to Spain when Joan Borrell, Josep's father, was eight years old.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:3-7)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-9) Borrell's father arrived in Spain just before the outbreak of the [Spanish Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Civil_War "Spanish Civil War") and afterwards he would never leave his village of La Pobla de Segur.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-10)

After completing primary education, the remote location of his village led Josep Borrell to be home-schooled with aid from his mother and a retired teacher, taking the official [Baccalaureate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Baccalaureate "Spanish Baccalaureate") exams at the [Lleida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lleida "Lleida") high school.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:3-7)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:2-11) He continued his higher education thanks to several scholarships, including from the [Juan March Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundaci%C3%B3n_Juan_March "Fundación Juan March") and the [Fulbright Program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulbright_Program "Fulbright Program").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:1-6)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:3-7)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-12)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-13) In 1964 he moved to [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcelona "Barcelona") to study industrial engineering, but left after a year in 1965 to study aeronautical engineering at the [Technical University of Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technical_University_of_Madrid "Technical University of Madrid") (UPM),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:3-7)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:2-11) graduating in 1969. In the summer of 1969 Borrell worked as volunteer at the [Gal On](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gal_On "Gal On")[kibbutz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kibbutz "Kibbutz") in Israel, where he met his future French wife Caroline Mayeur,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:3-7)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-14) from whom he is now divorced.

During this time, he also began to study for a bachelor's degree and later a PhD in economics at the [Complutense University of Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complutense_University "Complutense University") (UCM). Borrell also holds a master's degree in applied mathematics (operations research) from [Stanford University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford_University "Stanford University") in Palo Alto (California, US), and a postgraduate in energy economics from the [French Institute of Petroleum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Institute_of_Petroleum "French Institute of Petroleum") in Paris (France).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:3-7)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:0-15) In May 1976 Borrell defended his [PhD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_of_Philosophy "Doctor of Philosophy") thesis in economics at the [UCM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complutense_University_of_Madrid "Complutense University of Madrid").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:9-16)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:10-17)

From 1972 to 1982 he lectured in mathematics at the Higher Technical School of Aeronautical Engineering of the [UPM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polytechnic_University_of_Madrid "Polytechnic University of Madrid").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:0-15) In 1982 he was appointed associate professor of Business Mathematics at the [University of Valladolid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Valladolid "University of Valladolid").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-18) From 1975 to 1982 he also worked for [Cepsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cepsa "Cepsa"), employed at the company's Department of Systems and Information Engineering; he combined this activity with the teaching of university classes and involvement in local politics.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:2-11)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-19)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-20)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-21)

## Political career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Josep_Borrell&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Political career")]

### Involvement in local politics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Josep_Borrell&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Involvement in local politics")]

Borrell joined the [Spanish Socialist Workers' Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Socialist_Workers'_Party "Spanish Socialist Workers' Party") (PSOE) in 1975 and started his political activity during [Spain's transition to democracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_transition_to_democracy "Spanish transition to democracy") in the [Socialist Grouping of Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Socialist_Workers'_Party_of_the_Community_of_Madrid "Spanish Socialist Workers' Party of the Community of Madrid") along with [Luis Solana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Solana "Luis Solana") and [Luis Carlos Croissier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Carlos_Croissier "Luis Carlos Croissier").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-22)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-23)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-24) He ran for office as the number 5 in the PSOE list for the [1979 municipal election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1979_Spanish_local_elections "1979 Spanish local elections") in [Majadahonda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majadahonda "Majadahonda"), becoming city councillor. Borrell also became a member of the 1979–1983 corporation of the [Provincial Deputation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provincial_deputation_(Spain) "Provincial deputation (Spain)") of Madrid and managed the Financial Department of the provincial government body in the pre-autonomic period.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-25)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-26)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-27)

### Role during the González's governments

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Josep_Borrell&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Role during the González's governments")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/Eduardo_Sotillos_ofrece_la_rueda_de_prensa_posterior_al_Consejo_de_Ministros_junto_al_secretario_de_Estado_de_Hacienda._Pool_Moncloa._18_de_abril_de_1984.jpeg/250px-Eduardo_Sotillos_ofrece_la_rueda_de_prensa_posterior_al_Consejo_de_Ministros_junto_al_secretario_de_Estado_de_Hacienda._Pool_Moncloa._18_de_abril_de_1984.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Eduardo_Sotillos_ofrece_la_rueda_de_prensa_posterior_al_Consejo_de_Ministros_junto_al_secretario_de_Estado_de_Hacienda._Pool_Moncloa._18_de_abril_de_1984.jpeg)

Borrell, Secretary of State of Finance, next to [Eduardo Sotillos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eduardo_Sotillos "Eduardo Sotillos"), Spokesman of the Government, in [La Moncloa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Moncloa "La Moncloa"), 1984

In the [1982 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_Spanish_general_election "1982 Spanish general election") the PSOE won a landslide victory, returning the socialists to power for the first time since the years of the [Second Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Second_Republic "Spanish Second Republic").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-28)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-29) Under Prime Minister [Felipe González](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felipe_Gonz%C3%A1lez "Felipe González"), Borrell was appointed to several prominent positions within the Ministry of Economy and Finance, first as General Secretary for the Budget and Public Spending (1982–1984),[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-30) and then as [Secretary of State for Finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_State_for_Finance "Secretary of State for Finance") (1984–1991).[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-31)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-32) During his tenure as Secretary of State for Finance, Spain joined the [European Economic Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Economic_Community "European Economic Community") in 1986. He became known for his actions seeking to combat fraud and [tax evasion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_evasion "Tax evasion"), going after the rich and famous, including celebrities such as [Lola Flores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lola_Flores "Lola Flores"), [Marujita Díaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marujita_D%C3%ADaz "Marujita Díaz") or Pedro Ruiz.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-33)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-34)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-35)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-36) In the [1986 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Spanish_general_election "1986 Spanish general election") he was for the first time elected to the [Congress of Deputies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_Deputies "Congress of Deputies"), remaining as an [MP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_parliament "Member of parliament") representing [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcelona_(Spanish_Congress_Electoral_District) "Barcelona (Spanish Congress Electoral District)") until 2004.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-37)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-38)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-39)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-40)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-41)

In 1991 he joined the [Council of Ministers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_Ministers_(Spain) "Council of Ministers (Spain)") as [Minister of Public Works and Transport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_Public_Works_and_Transport "Minister of Public Works and Transport").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-42)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-43)

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/73/Rosa_Conde_en_la_rueda_de_prensa_posterior_al_Consejo_Ministros_con_el_ministro_de_Obras_P%C3%BAblicas_y_Transportes.jpg/250px-Rosa_Conde_en_la_rueda_de_prensa_posterior_al_Consejo_Ministros_con_el_ministro_de_Obras_P%C3%BAblicas_y_Transportes.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rosa_Conde_en_la_rueda_de_prensa_posterior_al_Consejo_Ministros_con_el_ministro_de_Obras_P%C3%BAblicas_y_Transportes.jpg)

In 1991, next to [Rosa Conde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosa_Conde "Rosa Conde"), during a joint press conference

He took a role in the process of [liberalization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberalization "Liberalization") of telecommunications in Spain,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-44) promoting the 1991–2001 National Plan of Telecommunications (PNT); in 1993, Borrell threatened nonetheless the [European Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Commission "European Commission") with blocking the liberalization unless the concession of a moratory Spain was given, as Borrell deemed imperative to achieve first the universalization of service before the complete liberalization.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-45)

Following the [1993 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_Spanish_general_election "1993 Spanish general election"), Borrell continued with a seat at the [Council of Ministers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_Ministers_(Spain) "Council of Ministers (Spain)"), assuming the portfolio of Minister of Public Works, Transport and Environment in the last government presided by Felipe González. He left the office after the arrival to power of the [People's Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Party_(Spain) "People's Party (Spain)") in 1996, remaining as an MP for Barcelona in the Spanish Congress.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Brief spell as leader of the opposition

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Josep_Borrell&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Brief spell as leader of the opposition")]

In 1998 Borrell decided to run against the [PSOE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Socialist_Workers'_Party "Spanish Socialist Workers' Party")'s then party leader [Joaquín Almunia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joaqu%C3%ADn_Almunia "Joaquín Almunia")[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-46) in the first national [primary election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_PSOE_prime_ministerial_primary "1998 PSOE prime ministerial primary") ever held in the PSOE since the [Second Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Spanish_Republic "Second Spanish Republic"),[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-47) intended to determine who the party would nominate as its prime ministerial candidate vis-à-vis the [2000 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Spanish_general_election "2000 Spanish general election"). Borrell ran as the underdog, campaigning as the candidate of the socialist base against the party establishment,[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-48)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-49)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-50)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-51)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-52) and surprisingly won the voting,[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-53) commanding 114,254 of the member's votes (54.99%), versus the 92,860 (44.67%) obtained by Almunia.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-54)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-55) Thus began an uneasy relationship and power-sharing—the "_bicefalia_" (_duumvirate_)—between the official party leader, Almunia, and the prime ministerial candidate elected by the members in the primaries, Borrell.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-56)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-57)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-58)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-59)

However, in May 1999, a fraud investigation was launched into two officials whom, several years earlier, Borrell had appointed to senior posts in the finance ministry. Though not involved in the inquiry into property purchases, Borrell resigned from the role of Prime Ministerial candidate, stating that he did not want the affair to damage his party's chances in the upcoming local and general elections.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-auto-5)

### Involvement in European politics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Josep_Borrell&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Involvement in European politics")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/Borrell_Portrait_2004.jpg/250px-Borrell_Portrait_2004.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Borrell_Portrait_2004.jpg)

Borrell's official portrait as President of the European Parliament, 2004

Amid the sixth term of the Cortes Generales, Borrell was elected to chair the [Joint Congress-Senate Committee on the European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Congress-Senate_Committee_on_the_European_Union "Joint Congress-Senate Committee on the European Union") in October 1999,[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-elpais-60) replacing [Pedro Solbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_Solbes "Pedro Solbes"). Reelected as [MP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_parliament "Member of parliament") for Barcelona in the [2000 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Spanish_general_election "2000 Spanish general election"), Borrell repeated as president of the Joint Committee for the European Union for the full 7th parliamentary term.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-elpais-60)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:5-61)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:6-62) Then, in 2001, Borrell was also appointed the [Spanish parliament's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cortes_Generales "Cortes Generales") representative on the [Convention on the Future of Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convention_on_the_Future_of_Europe "Convention on the Future of Europe").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-auto-5)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:5-61)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:6-62) In 2011 he was awarded Spain's medal of the [Order of Constitutional Merit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Constitutional_Merit "Order of Constitutional Merit") in recognition of his participation in this convention, which drafted the [European Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_establishing_a_Constitution_for_Europe "Treaty establishing a Constitution for Europe") that eventually led to the [Treaty of Lisbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Lisbon "Treaty of Lisbon").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:4-63) During his time at the convention, he unsuccessfully pushed for a mention to a "federal model" in the draft, as well as he advocated for the explicit mention of the equality between women and men. A laicist, he also then opposed the inclusion of the notion of a "Christian heritage" in the text.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-64)

In 2004, the prime minister and PSOE's leader [José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Luis_Rodr%C3%ADguez_Zapatero "José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero") proposed Borrell to lead the Socialist Ticket in the [2004 European elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_European_Parliament_election_in_Spain "2004 European Parliament election in Spain").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-65) The PSOE won the elections with 6,6 million votes (43,30%), obtaining 25 MEP seats, although turnout was relatively low at 46%.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-66)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-67) Borrell sat with the [Party of European Socialists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_of_European_Socialists "Party of European Socialists") (PES) group, and served as leader of the Spanish delegation.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In July 2004 Borrell was elected [President of the European Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_European_Parliament "President of the European Parliament"), as a result of an agreement between the [EPP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_People's_Party_group "European People's Party group") and the [Socialists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_Alliance_of_Socialists_and_Democrats "Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats"), becoming the third Spaniard to hold this position after [Enrique Barón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enrique_Bar%C3%B3n_Crespo "Enrique Barón Crespo") and [José María Gil-Robles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mar%C3%ADa_Gil-Robles "José María Gil-Robles").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-68)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-69)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-70) In the presidential vote, out of 700 [Members of the European Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Members_of_the_European_Parliament "Members of the European Parliament") (MEPs) he received an absolute majority with 388 votes in the first ballot. The other two candidates were the Polish Liberal [Bronisław Geremek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronis%C5%82aw_Geremek "Bronisław Geremek") (208 votes) and the French communist [Francis Wurtz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Wurtz "Francis Wurtz") (51 votes).[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-71) He was the first newly elected MEP to hold the post since direct elections were held in 1979.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-72) As part of a deal with the conservative faction in the parliament, the [EPP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_People's_Party_European_Democrats "European People's Party European Democrats"), he was succeeded as president of the parliament by the German conservative politician [Hans-Gert Pöttering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hans-Gert_P%C3%B6ttering "Hans-Gert Pöttering") in the second part of the five-year term.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-73)

In his capacity as president, Borrell also chaired the Parliament's temporary committee on policy challenges and budgetary means of the enlarged Union 2007–2013. From 2007 until leaving the Parliament in 2009,[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-auto1-74) he served as chairman of the [Committee on Development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Committee_on_Development "Committee on Development"). In addition to his committee assignments, he was a member of the Parliament's delegation to the [ACP–EU Joint Parliamentary Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACP%E2%80%93EU_Joint_Parliamentary_Assembly "ACP–EU Joint Parliamentary Assembly").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Step back from the political front

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Josep_Borrell&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Step back from the political front")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b0/08.10.2017_Manifestaci%C3%B3_%22Prou%21_Recuperem_el_seny%22_-_Barcelona_19_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-08.10.2017_Manifestaci%C3%B3_%22Prou%21_Recuperem_el_seny%22_-_Barcelona_19_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:08.10.2017_Manifestaci%C3%B3_%22Prou!_Recuperem_el_seny%22_-_Barcelona_19_(cropped).jpg)

Borrell holding an [EU flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EU_flag "EU flag"), between [Mario Vargas Llosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Vargas_Llosa "Mario Vargas Llosa") and [Albert Rivera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Rivera "Albert Rivera") during a mass rally defending the unity of Spain held in Barcelona on 8 October 2017

Borrell was nominated president of the [European University Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_University_Institute "European University Institute") on 12 December 2008, and assumed this position in January 2010. In 2012, he was forced to resign after failing to disclose a financial relationship with [Abengoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abengoa "Abengoa"), which paid him €300,000 yearly as a board member for the company.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-auto1-74)

In 2012, the [University of Lleida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Lleida "University of Lleida") appointed Borrell to a professorship of competition and regional development sponsored by energy company [Repsol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Repsol "Repsol").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-auto1-74) He also held the Jean Monnet Chair at the Institute of International Studies at [Complutense University of Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complutense_University_of_Madrid "Complutense University of Madrid"). [_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Borrell collaborated along with other prominent PSOE figures, such as [Cristina Narbona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristina_Narbona "Cristina Narbona"), [José Félix Tezanos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_F%C3%A9lix_Tezanos "José Félix Tezanos") and [Manuel Escudero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Escudero "Manuel Escudero"), in the making of _Somos socialistas. Por una nueva socialdemocracia_ ("We are socialists. For a new social-democracy"), a manifesto in support of [Pedro Sánchez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_S%C3%A1nchez "Pedro Sánchez")'s successful bid to the leadership of the PSOE in the [May 2017 PSOE primary election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Spanish_Socialist_Workers'_Party_leadership_election "2017 Spanish Socialist Workers' Party leadership election") prior to the 39th Federal Congress of the party.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-75)

He also stood out as one of the most outspoken opponents of [Catalan secessionism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalan_independence_movement "Catalan independence movement"). Borrell co-authored _Las cuentas y los cuentos de la independencia_ ("The calculations and tales behind independence"), a 2015 essay that vowed to dismantle the economic arguments laid out by the pro-independence movement.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-76) He also took a leading role in a mass rally defending the unity of Spain held in Barcelona on 8 October 2017, in which Borrell gave an impassionated speech demanding "not to bring up more frontiers" while displaying a European Union flag that he called "our _[estelada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estelada "Estelada")_" (starred flag),[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-77)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-78)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-79) bringing him back to the media first line.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-80)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-81) He also took part on a second mass rally on 29 October 2017 under the slogan "We are all Catalonia".[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-82)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-83)

### Foreign Minister, 2018–2019

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Josep_Borrell&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Foreign Minister, 2018–2019")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/75/Primer_Gobierno_de_Pedro_S%C3%A1nchez_%282018-10%29.jpg/250px-Primer_Gobierno_de_Pedro_S%C3%A1nchez_%282018-10%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Primer_Gobierno_de_Pedro_S%C3%A1nchez_(2018-10).jpg)

Group photo presenting the new Council of Ministers at [La Moncloa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moncloa_Palace "Moncloa Palace") (June 2018)

Following the [2018 successful motion of no confidence against Mariano Rajoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_vote_of_no_confidence_in_the_government_of_Mariano_Rajoy "2018 vote of no confidence in the government of Mariano Rajoy") and subsequent investiture of [Pedro Sánchez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_S%C3%A1nchez "Pedro Sánchez") as new prime minister, Borrell was announced on 5 June as Sánchez's choice for the post of foreign minister in [his new government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A1nchez_I_Government "Sánchez I Government").[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-84) 22 years after the end of his last tenure as member of the [Government of Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Spain "Government of Spain"), Borrell assumed the portfolio of [Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Foreign_Affairs_(Spain) "Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Spain)") on 7 June along the rest of the new cabinet in [La Zarzuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zarzuela_Palace "Zarzuela Palace").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-85) The new minister relocated some of the high-rank officials appointed by the government of Mariano Rajoy with a diplomatic background to ambassadorial posts, including secretaries of State and, most notably, the former foreign minister ([Alfonso Dastis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfonso_Dastis "Alfonso Dastis")) and the [prime minister's chief of staff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moncloa_Chief_of_Staff "Moncloa Chief of Staff") ([Jorge Moragas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Moragas "Jorge Moragas")).[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-86)

Borrell decided to reformulate the High Commissioner for the 'Marca España' (Spain Brand), a one-person body functionally dependent directly on the Office of the Prime Minister but organically included within the Foreign Office structure to the post of [Secretary of State for Global Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_State_for_Global_Spain "Secretary of State for Global Spain").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-87) The officeholder responsible for the 'Marca España' since 2012, The [Marquess of Valtierra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Espinosa_de_los_Monteros_y_Bernaldo_de_Quir%C3%B3s "Carlos Espinosa de los Monteros y Bernaldo de Quirós"), was replaced by [Irene Lozano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irene_Lozano "Irene Lozano").[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-88)

In June 2018, Borrell accompanied [King Felipe VI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Felipe_VI "King Felipe VI") on an official visit to the US.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-89) Borrell had a meeting with [Mike Pompeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo "Mike Pompeo"), where the Spanish delegation expressed concern over the US protectionist drift; discrepancies were found between the two countries in their approach to migration policies.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-90)

In September 2018, the [National Securities Market Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Securities_Market_Commission "National Securities Market Commission") (CNMV) settled a disciplinary action against Borrell opened in 2017 due to the latter's [insider trading](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insider_trading "Insider trading") in the sale of stocks of [Abengoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abengoa "Abengoa") (whose [board of directors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_directors "Board of directors") Borrell was a member of) in November 2015, sanctioning him with a fine of 30,000€.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-91)[[n. 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-93)

Regarding the negotiations with the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") on [Gibraltar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibraltar "Gibraltar") in the context of [Brexit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brexit "Brexit"), Borrell vowed to prioritise improvement of the living conditions in neighbouring [Campo de Gibraltar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campo_de_Gibraltar "Campo de Gibraltar")[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-elespanol-94) (he reportedly considered the reality of the "3rd territory with the highest GDP per capita in the World"—Gibraltar—surrounded by "a flatland of underdevelopment"—the Campo de Gibraltar—as something unacceptable).[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-95)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-96) On the other hand, he renounced attempts to include the longstanding bid for sovereignty as an element of the negotiations.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-elespanol-94) Borrell highlighted the fact that this soft approach was the same stance used by his predecessor, Dastis, outlining a continuity in the negotiations with the former government, with the ministry keeping the same negotiating team as before the government change.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-97)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-98) In November 2018, he signed four [MoUs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memorandum_of_understanding "Memorandum of understanding") negotiated with the United Kingdom, settling aspects of the future relationship with the [British Overseas Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Overseas_Territories "British Overseas Territories").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-99)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/El_presidente_del_Gobierno%2C_Pedro_S%C3%A1nchez%2C_en_Estrasburgo_02.jpg/250px-El_presidente_del_Gobierno%2C_Pedro_S%C3%A1nchez%2C_en_Estrasburgo_02.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:El_presidente_del_Gobierno,_Pedro_S%C3%A1nchez,_en_Estrasburgo_02.jpg)

Borrell (centre) with [PES](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_of_European_Socialists "Party of European Socialists")_Spitzenkandidat_[Frans Timmermans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frans_Timmermans "Frans Timmermans") and [Pedro Sánchez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_S%C3%A1nchez "Pedro Sánchez") in January 2019

Given the aggravation of the [political crisis in Nicaragua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%932022_Nicaraguan_protests "2018–2022 Nicaraguan protests"), in December 2018 Borrell pressed EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs [Federica Mogherini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federica_Mogherini "Federica Mogherini") for EU-wide involvement in the situation.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-100)

In May 2019, the [Spanish Embassy in Caracas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embassy_of_Spain,_Caracas "Embassy of Spain, Caracas") lodged Venezuelan dissident [Leopoldo López](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leopoldo_L%C3%B3pez "Leopoldo López") as a guest following the [Venezuelan uprising](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Venezuelan_uprising_attempt "2019 Venezuelan uprising attempt"), as the latter had been freed from domiciliary imprisonment by forces endorsing [Juan Guaidó](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Guaid%C3%B3 "Juan Guaidó"). However, Borrell warned Spain was not going "to allow the embassy to become a centre of political activism", vowing to restrict the political activities of López as a guest.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-101)

For the [2019 European Parliament election in Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_European_Parliament_election_in_Spain "2019 European Parliament election in Spain"), Borrell ran first in the PSOE list.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-102) During the electoral campaign, he appealed to the unity of Europe and stressed the need for EU member states to pool sovereignty in order to survive as a civilization.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-103) Shortly after his election, he gave up his newly won seat before the inaugural session of the legislature, arguing that acting prime minister Pedro Sánchez and he had agreed that, amid the uncertainty regarding the second investiture of Sánchez, the post of foreign minister should not be left vacant for an indefinite period.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-104)

In October 2019, Borrell condemned the [Turkish offensive into north-eastern Syria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Turkish_offensive_into_north-eastern_Syria "2019 Turkish offensive into north-eastern Syria") against [Syrian Kurds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_Administration_of_North_and_East_Syria "Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria"), adding that "We don't have magic powers" to stop the Turkish invasion.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-105)

He stepped down from the office on 29 November 2019 and was succeeded _ad interim_ by the [Minister of Defence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Defence_(Spain) "Ministry of Defence (Spain)"), [Margarita Robles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margarita_Robles "Margarita Robles").[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-106)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-107)

### European Union High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Josep_Borrell&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: European Union High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy")]

#### 2019

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Josep_Borrell&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2019")]

On 2 July 2019, [President of the European Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_European_Council "President of the European Council")[Donald Tusk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Tusk "Donald Tusk") announced that the [European Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Council "European Council") would nominate Josep Borrell as [High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Representative_of_the_Union_for_Foreign_Affairs_and_Security_Policy "High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-108) The portfolio had been reportedly beefed up with additional responsibilities in [humanitarian aid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humanitarian_aid "Humanitarian aid"), support of development policies in Africa and the external dimension of immigration.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-109) Also in July 2019, he announced the acquisition of double Argentine–Spanish citizenship, assumed on 18 July 2019, thus gaining the citizenship his father was born with.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-110)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-111) He passed the hearing before the [European Parliament Committee on Foreign Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Parliament_Committee_on_Foreign_Affairs "European Parliament Committee on Foreign Affairs") (AFET) on 7 October 2019. His nomination was green-lighted the next day by a vote of AFET members.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-112)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-113)

To counter its negative image in the EU, [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") sent medical aid and supplies to EU countries affected by the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-114) Borrell warned that there is "a geopolitical component, including a struggle for influence through spinning and the 'politics of generosity'." He also said that "China is aggressively pushing the message that, unlike the US, it is a responsible and reliable partner."[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-115)

#### 2020

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Josep_Borrell&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2020")]

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/99/Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_with_European_Union_High_Representative_Borrell_%2849500956328%29.jpg/250px-Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_with_European_Union_High_Representative_Borrell_%2849500956328%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretary_Pompeo_Meets_with_European_Union_High_Representative_Borrell_(49500956328).jpg)

Borrell with U.S. Secretary of State [Mike Pompeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo "Mike Pompeo") on 7 February 2020

Borrell said that [proposed Israeli annexation of the West Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proposed_Israeli_annexation_of_the_West_Bank "Proposed Israeli annexation of the West Bank") "could not pass unchallenged" and warned that "failure to adequately respond would encourage other states with territorial claims to disregard basic principles of international law".[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-116)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-117) He said that "In line with international law and relevant U.N. Security Council resolutions, the EU does not recognize Israel's sovereignty" over the [Palestinian territories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_territories "Palestinian territories") occupied since 1967.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-118) Borrell hailed the [peace agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93United_Arab_Emirates_peace_agreement "Israel–United Arab Emirates peace agreement") between [Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel") and the [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates") as benefiting both nations and being important for stability in the Middle East. He also called Israeli suspension of its annexation plans positive and stated that the European Union hoped for a [two-state solution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-state_solution "Two-state solution").[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-119)

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bb/Josep_Borrell_Fontelles_and_Recep_Tayyip_Erdo%C4%9Fan_in_Turkey.jpg/250px-Josep_Borrell_Fontelles_and_Recep_Tayyip_Erdo%C4%9Fan_in_Turkey.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Josep_Borrell_Fontelles_and_Recep_Tayyip_Erdo%C4%9Fan_in_Turkey.jpg)

Borrell and Turkish President [Recep Tayyip Erdoğan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recep_Tayyip_Erdo%C4%9Fan "Recep Tayyip Erdoğan") at the [South-East European Cooperation Process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South-East_European_Cooperation_Process "South-East European Cooperation Process") (SEECP) Summit in Antalya, Turkey on 17 June 2021

On 9 April 2020, Borrell, on behalf of the EU, with the release of the first report of the Investigation and Identification Team to the Executive Council of the [Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisation_for_the_Prohibition_of_Chemical_Weapons "Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons") and to the [Secretary-General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary-General_of_the_United_Nations "Secretary-General of the United Nations") of the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") on 8 April 2020, declared that "We fully support the report's findings and note with great concern its conclusions. The European Union strongly condemns the use of chemical weapons by the [Syrian Arab Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_Air_Force "Syrian Air Force") as concluded by the report. Those identified as responsible for the use of chemical weapons must be held accountable for these reprehensible acts."[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-120)

On 24 April, the EU's foreign security policy agency, the [European External Action Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_External_Action_Service "European External Action Service") (EEAS), published a report on [disinformation related to the COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misinformation_related_to_the_COVID-19_pandemic "Misinformation related to the COVID-19 pandemic"). _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ reported that the language had been toned down amid [criticism from China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China%E2%80%93European_Union_relations "China–European Union relations"). The final report differed in key areas from both an internal version and an earlier draft planned for public release. At a parliamentary hearing on 30 April, Borrell acknowledged that China had expressed concerns about the report after it leaked, but he denied the EU had bowed to pressure or that the report had been revised.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-121) Borrell said that there were two separate reports, one for internal consumption and one for publication. Responding to questions from members of the European Parliament, Borrell accused staff of damaging the EU by leaking. He also appeared to suggest that analysts' views were biased and cast doubt on their credibility: "I cannot accept that the personal belief or feeling of a member of staff leaking mails—maybe being written to be leaked—created damage to the credibility of the institution", he said, later asking MEPs why "more credibility" was being given "to the personal opinion of a member of a staff". [_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Multiple EU officials told [BuzzFeed News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BuzzFeed_News "BuzzFeed News") and _The New York Times_ that they were angry and disappointed by Borrell's focus on leaks and, in particular, his singling out of junior staff members.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-bf1-122)

Concerning the long-standing [Aegean dispute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aegean_dispute "Aegean dispute") between Turkey and Greece, Borrell in August 2020 expressed "full solidarity" with [Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greece "Greece") and [Cyprus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyprus "Cyprus") (Turkey has [occupied northern Cyprus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_invasion_of_Cyprus "Turkish invasion of Cyprus") since July 1974)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-123) and called for "immediate deescalation" by Turkey and "reengaging in dialogue."[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-124)

#### 2021

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bf/04_11_2021_Reuni%C3%A3o_com_o_representante_para_Pol%C3%ADtica_Externa_e_de_Seguran%C3%A7a_da_Uni%C3%A3o_Europeia_e_Vice-Presidente_da_Comiss%C3%A3o_Europeia%2C_Josep_Borrell_Fontelles_%2851657378193%29.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:04_11_2021_Reuni%C3%A3o_com_o_representante_para_Pol%C3%ADtica_Externa_e_de_Seguran%C3%A7a_da_Uni%C3%A3o_Europeia_e_Vice-Presidente_da_Comiss%C3%A3o_Europeia,_Josep_Borrell_Fontelles_(51657378193).jpg)

In February 2021, Borrell voiced "strong concern" about China's "treatment of ethnic and religious minorities, in particular" ethnic [Uyghurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uyghurs "Uyghurs") in [Xinjiang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xinjiang "Xinjiang").[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-126) In March 2021, he said China's [sanctions on EU officials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China%E2%80%93European_Union_relations "China–European Union relations") had created "a new atmosphere" and "a new situation".[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-127)

Borrell with Serbian President [Aleksandar Vučić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aleksandar_Vu%C4%8Di%C4%87 "Aleksandar Vučić") on 11 November 2022

Although warned against doing so by several EU countries, Borrell decided on his own initiative to make the first high-level EU trip of its type in four years to Russia amidst the [2021 Russian protests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Russian_protests "2021 Russian protests"), to meet with [Russian Foreign Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_Foreign_Affairs_(Russia) "Minister of Foreign Affairs (Russia)")[Sergey Lavrov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergey_Lavrov "Sergey Lavrov"). The visit was described by [MEPs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_the_European_Parliament "Member of the European Parliament"), diplomats and other political observers as a humiliation for Borrell, as he stood by while Lavrov called the EU an "unreliable partner" and Russia expelled three EU diplomats while Borrell and Lavrov held their joint press briefing.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-128)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-129)[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-130) This led to a group of over 70 MEPs to call for Borrell's resignation.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-131)

In May 2021, Borrell called for a [ceasefire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Israel%E2%80%93Palestine_crisis "2021 Israel–Palestine crisis") between Israel and the Palestinian [Islamist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamist "Islamist") group [Hamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamas "Hamas").[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-132)

In June 2021, the Spanish newspaper [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_(newspaper) "ABC (newspaper)") published a mail that described that Borrell had informed the Cuban embassy about the debate in the European Parliament about the situation in [Cuba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba "Cuba") and that showed his intention to stop the debate and prevent it from reaching the Parliament's floor. A group of at least 16 MEPs asked Borrell for explanations.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-133)

In August 2021, Borrell received criticism for sending a high-ranking EU representative, [Enrique Mora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enrique_Mora "Enrique Mora"), to attend the inauguration of [Iranian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran "Iran") president [Ebrahim Raisi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ebrahim_Raisi "Ebrahim Raisi"). Mora was seated directly behind senior leaders of [Hamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamas "Hamas") and [Hezbollah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hezbollah "Hezbollah") during the ceremony.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-inauguration-134) Borrell's decision to send him there was blasted by [David Lega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Lega "David Lega") and eight other [members of the European Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_the_European_Parliament "Member of the European Parliament") who sent Borrell a letter stating that his action "contradicts European commitments to uphold and stand for human rights." The MEPs also pointed to Raisi's role in the [1988 executions of Iranian political prisoners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_executions_of_Iranian_political_prisoners "1988 executions of Iranian political prisoners") and warned that honoring the "inauguration of the 'Hangman of Tehran' only serves to encourage such behavior".[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-inauguration-134)

In September 2021, Borrell compared the situation on the [Belarus–Poland border](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belarus%E2%80%93Poland_border "Belarus–Poland border") to the migrant crisis on the [Morocco–Spain border](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morocco%E2%80%93Spain_border "Morocco–Spain border").[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-135)

In October 2021, he went to [Saudi Arabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia "Saudi Arabia") after visiting [Qatar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qatar "Qatar") and the [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates").[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-136) Borrell said that the EU "now has human rights dialogues with all Gulf States and we launched such a dialogue with Saudi Arabia this week. This is an area where there is much to gain for both sides from closer cooperation."[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-137) Borrell and Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister [Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faisal_bin_Farhan_Al_Saud "Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud") also discussed the conflict in [Yemen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yemen "Yemen") and the humanitarian situation in [Taliban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taliban "Taliban")-controlled [Afghanistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghanistan "Afghanistan"). Borell described the situation in Yemen as a "terrible tragedy" and called for a peaceful solution to the [war in Yemen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yemeni_civil_war_(2014%E2%80%93present) "Yemeni civil war (2014–present)"), which is largely seen in the region as a [proxy conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran%E2%80%93Saudi_Arabia_proxy_conflict "Iran–Saudi Arabia proxy conflict") between Iran and Saudi Arabia.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-138)

On 8 October 2021, Borrell said the EU's [relations with Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey%E2%80%93European_Union_relations "Turkey–European Union relations") has significantly improved and he called his relationship with Turkish President [Recep Tayyip Erdoğan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recep_Tayyip_Erdo%C4%9Fan "Recep Tayyip Erdoğan") "excellent".[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-139)

On 18 October 2021, Borrell argued that the [2021 global energy crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_global_energy_crisis "2021 global energy crisis") had "deep geopolitical roots. ... the price of gas, the scarcity, is something that has to be looked at from a geopolitical perspective."[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-140)

In December 2021, he criticised EU member states for not imposing sanctions on [Ethiopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia "Ethiopia"), which was accused of [war crimes during the Tigray War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_crimes_in_the_Tigray_War "War crimes in the Tigray War"). Borrell said the situation in Ethiopia was "one of my biggest frustrations" of the year because the EU was not able to react properly to the large-scale human rights violations, "mass rapes using sexual violence as a war arm, killings and concentration camps based on ethnic belonging."[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-141)

#### 2022

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Josep_Borrell&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: 2022")]

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/Parliament_call_for_massive_increase_of_military_assistance_to_Ukraine_-_52408865825.jpg/250px-Parliament_call_for_massive_increase_of_military_assistance_to_Ukraine_-_52408865825.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Parliament_call_for_massive_increase_of_military_assistance_to_Ukraine_-_52408865825.jpg)

Borrell speaks to the [European Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Parliament "European Parliament") in 2022.

On 22 February 2022, after Russia recognised the breakaway [Donetsk People's Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donetsk_People's_Republic "Donetsk People's Republic") and [Lugansk People's Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lugansk_People's_Republic "Lugansk People's Republic") and subsequently sent troops into the two regions, Borrell issued a statement condemning the actions and called upon Russia to return to the tenets of the [Normandy Format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normandy_Format "Normandy Format").[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-142) Following the [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine") on 24 February, Borrell and European Commission president [Ursula von der Leyen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ursula_von_der_Leyen "Ursula von der Leyen") were part of an EU delegation visiting Kyiv on 8 April.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-143) Borrell said he wants EU countries to confiscate frozen [foreign-exchange reserves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_foreign-exchange_reserves "List of countries by foreign-exchange reserves") of the Russian central bank—which amount to over $300 billion—to cover the costs of rebuilding Ukraine after the war.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-144)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-145)

In September 2022, he welcomed a [UN report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN_Human_Rights_Office_report_on_Xinjiang "UN Human Rights Office report on Xinjiang") on the [human rights abuses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persecution_of_Uyghurs_in_China "Persecution of Uyghurs in China") of the [Uyghur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uyghurs "Uyghurs") minority in China.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-146)

On 13 October 2022, when speaking at the European Diplomatic Academy's inauguration ceremony in Bruges, Belgium, Borrell declared that "Europe is a garden and the rest of the world is a jungle." He added that the garden could be invaded by the jungle and that the gardeners would need to travel there in order to defend it.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-147) On 18 October, in response to his comments, the [Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Foreign_Affairs_and_International_Cooperation_(United_Arab_Emirates) "Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (United Arab Emirates)") summoned the acting head of the EU mission at UAE to explain Borrell's remarks, stating that the remarks were "inappropriate and discriminatory" and "contribute to a worsening climate of intolerance and discrimination worldwide."[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-148)

On 3 June 2023, [Indonesian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesia "Indonesia") Defense Minister [Prabowo Subianto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prabowo_Subianto "Prabowo Subianto") proposed a multi-point [peace plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_negotiations_in_the_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Peace negotiations in the Russian invasion of Ukraine") for the [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Russian invasion of Ukraine"), calling for a ceasefire, a demilitarized zone observed and monitored by [UN peacekeepers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_Nations_peacekeeping_missions "List of United Nations peacekeeping missions"), and a U.N. referendum in what he called "disputed territory".[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-151)[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-152) Borrell criticized Prabow's proposal, saying that "We need to bring peace to Ukraine", but it must be a "just peace, not a peace of surrender."[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-153)

On 21 September 2023, Borrell released a statement which condemned the [military operation by Azerbaijan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Azerbaijani_offensive_in_Nagorno-Karabakh "2023 Azerbaijani offensive in Nagorno-Karabakh") against the Armenian population of [Nagorno-Karabakh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagorno-Karabakh "Nagorno-Karabakh") and deplored the casualties and loss of life caused by the offensive.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-154)

He condemned the "barbaric and terrorist attack" by [Hamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamas "Hamas") on Israel, which started the [Gaza war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war "Gaza war"). On 10 October 2023, Borrell accused Israel of breaking international law by imposing a [blockade of the Gaza Strip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_2023_Israeli_blockade_of_the_Gaza_Strip "October 2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip").[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-155) On 3 January 2024, he condemned the comments of the Israeli ministers [Itamar Ben-Gvir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itamar_Ben-Gvir "Itamar Ben-Gvir") and [Bezalel Smotrich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezalel_Smotrich "Bezalel Smotrich"), writing, "Forced displacements are strictly prohibited as a grave violation of [international humanitarian law] & words matter."[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-156)[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-157)[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-158) In March 2024, Borrell said Israel's depriving food from Palestinians was a serious violation of international humanitarian law, and described the [Flour massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flour_massacre "Flour massacre") as "totally unacceptable carnage".[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-159) German Chancellor [Olaf Scholz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olaf_Scholz "Olaf Scholz") confronted Borrell over his months-long criticism of Israel, saying Borrell did not speak for Germany.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-160)

#### 2024

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Josep_Borrell&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: 2024")]

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fa/Josep_Borrell_Fontelles_and_Kassym-Jomart_Tokayev_%28P064258-39523%29.jpg/250px-Josep_Borrell_Fontelles_and_Kassym-Jomart_Tokayev_%28P064258-39523%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Josep_Borrell_Fontelles_and_Kassym-Jomart_Tokayev_(P064258-39523).jpg)

Borrell with President of Kazakhstan [Kassym-Jomart Tokayev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kassym-Jomart_Tokayev "Kassym-Jomart Tokayev") in Astana, 1 August 2024

In April 2024, Borrell "strongly condemned" the [Iranian strikes on Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/April_2024_Iranian_strikes_against_Israel "April 2024 Iranian strikes against Israel"), calling them "an unprecedented escalation and a grave threat to regional security".[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-161) Previously in March 2024, Borrell had stalled efforts by nine EU foreign ministers to sanction Iran over its missile and drone program, because he felt that new sanctions might hamper efforts to bind Iran to a nuclear non-proliferation deal.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-162)

On 15 May 2024, Borrell called on Israel to immediately halt its [assault on Rafah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafah_offensive "Rafah offensive"), stating it was disrupting humanitarian aid and causing a humanitarian crisis, while also calling on Hamas to release all [Israeli hostages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war_hostage_crisis "Gaza war hostage crisis").[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-163) Borrell condemned the [Tel al-Sultan attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tel_al-Sultan_attack "Tel al-Sultan attack"), saying that Israel's military actions needed to stop.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-164)

## Post Brussels, 2025–present

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Josep_Borrell&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Post Brussels, 2025–present")]

In May 2025, after his retirement as an EU diplomat, Borrell spoke out against Israel's actions, accusing Israel of committing [genocide in Gaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_genocide "Gaza genocide").[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-165) After the [2026 United States strikes in Venezuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_strikes_in_Venezuela "2026 United States strikes in Venezuela"), Borrell advocated for greater strategic independence for Europe from the United States and described [Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump "Trump")'s actions as a clear violation of [international law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_law "International law").[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-166)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Josep_Borrell&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Personal life")]

[![Image 27](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/95/Recepci%C3%B3n_al_Cuerpo_Diplom%C3%A1tico_2019_03_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Recepci%C3%B3n_al_Cuerpo_Diplom%C3%A1tico_2019_03_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Recepci%C3%B3n_al_Cuerpo_Diplom%C3%A1tico_2019_03_(cropped).jpg)

Josep Borrell and Cristina Narbona during a reception of the Diplomatic Corps in 2019

Borrell was first married to French sociologist Carolina Mayeur. The marriage produced two sons: Joan, a diplomat, and Lionel, an aircraft pilot.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-mellado-184) Borrell and Mayeur divorced in the 1990s. [_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Since 1998, Borrell has been in a relationship with [Cristina Narbona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristina_Narbona "Cristina Narbona"), a Spanish [PSOE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PSOE "PSOE") politician and former Minister of Environment (2004–2008) in the [Zapatero administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zapatero_administration "Zapatero administration").[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-bio-185) The couple, resident in [Valdemorillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valdemorillo "Valdemorillo") since 2001, married in July 2018.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-mellado-184)[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-186)

In 2019, he acquired [Argentine citizenship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentine_nationality_law "Argentine nationality law") through descent, stating that he wished to honour the memory of his father, who grew up in [Mendoza, Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mendoza,_Argentina "Mendoza, Argentina").[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-187)

Borrell speaks [Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language"), [Catalan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalan_language "Catalan language"), [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language"), [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language") and [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_language "English language").[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-188)

He has been a keen participant in the annual festivity in his native [Pobla de Segur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pobla_de_Segur "Pobla de Segur") descending the [Noguera Pallaresa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noguera_Pallaresa "Noguera Pallaresa") river, in which the stream is rowed down by the partakers as [log drivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Log_driving "Log driving") (_raiers_).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-pobladesegur-3)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-:3-7)[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-189)

### Corrupt share dealing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Josep_Borrell&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Corrupt share dealing")]

In November 2018, the national stock market regulator in Spain concluded that Borrell traded shares of the company Abengoa while in possession of insider information.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-euo1-190) Borrell was fined €30,000 for the breach.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josep_Borrell#cite_note-191)
