There are multiple services under its authority, along with that of some other ministers. Under the authority of the Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Development, that of Cooperation and European Affairs, and that of Foreign and European Affairs, there are numerous services directly related to the ministers. Here is a list of those services.

*   The ministers' cabinet
*   The office of cabinets, which gathers a personnel in charge of the administrative and logistics aspects of the three ministers' cabinets
*   The budget control service (_CBCM_)
*   General inspection of foreign affairs (_IGAE_)
*   The prospective office (_DP_)
*   The Protocole, upon which the President's protocol cell relies
*   The Crisis management Department (_CDC_)

The **Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs** ([French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"): _Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères_[[ministɛʁ də løʁɔp e dez‿afɛʁ(z‿)etʁɑ̃ʒɛʁ]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French "Help:IPA/French"), **MEAE**) is the [ministry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_(government_department) "Ministry (government department)") of the [Government of France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_France "Government of France") that handles France's [foreign relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_relations "Foreign relations"). Since 1855, its headquarters have been located at 37 [Quai d'Orsay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quai_d'Orsay "Quai d'Orsay"), close to the [National Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Assembly_(France) "National Assembly (France)"). The term **Quai d'Orsay** is often used as a [metonym](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metonymy "Metonymy") for the ministry. Its cabinet minister, the **minister for Europe and foreign affairs** ([French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"): _Ministre de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères_) is responsible for the [foreign relations of France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_relations_of_France "Foreign relations of France"). The current officeholder, [Jean-Noël Barrot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-No%C3%ABl_Barrot "Jean-Noël Barrot"), was appointed in September 2024. For a brief period from 1984 to 1986, the office was titled **minister for external relations**.

In 1547, royal secretaries became specialised, writing correspondence to foreign governments and negotiating peace treaties. The four French [secretaries of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_state "Secretary of state") where foreign relations were divided by region, in 1589, became centralised with one becoming first secretary responsible for international relations. The [Ancien Régime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancien_R%C3%A9gime "Ancien Régime") position of [Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_State_for_Foreign_Affairs_(France) "Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs (France)") became Foreign Minister around 1723;[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_Ministers_of_France#cite_note-1) it was renamed Minister of Foreign Affairs in 1791 in the aftermath of early stages of the [French Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Revolution "French Revolution"). All ministerial positions were abolished in 1794 by the [National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Convention "National Convention") and reestablished with the [Directory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Directory "French Directory").

Foreign Affairs Ministry building on the [Quai d'Orsay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quai_d'Orsay "Quai d'Orsay")

There are multiple services under its authority, along with that of some other ministers. Under the authority of the Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Development, that of Cooperation and European Affairs, and that of Foreign and European Affairs, there are numerous services directly related to the ministers. Here is a list of those services.

*   The ministers' cabinet
*   The office of cabinets, which gathers a personnel in charge of the administrative and logistics aspects of the three ministers' cabinets
*   The budget control service (_CBCM_)
*   General inspection of foreign affairs (_IGAE_)
*   The prospective office (_DP_)
*   The Protocole, upon which the President's protocol cell relies
*   The Crisis management Department (_CDC_)

**Bernard Kouchner** (born 1 November 1939) is a French politician and doctor. He is the co-founder of [Médecins Sans Frontières](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A9decins_Sans_Fronti%C3%A8res "Médecins Sans Frontières") (MSF) and [Médecins du Monde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A9decins_du_Monde "Médecins du Monde"). From 2007 until 2010, he was the French [Minister of Foreign and European Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_Foreign_Affairs_(France) "Minister of Foreign Affairs (France)") in the center-right [Fillon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Fillon "François Fillon") government under president [Nicolas Sarkozy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolas_Sarkozy "Nicolas Sarkozy"), although he had been in the past a minister in socialist governments and was himself a long-term member of the [Socialist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_Party_(France) "Socialist Party (France)"). 2010, _[The Jerusalem Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Jerusalem\_Post "The Jerusalem Post")_ considered Kouchner the 15th most influential Jew in the world.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-1) Since 2015 Kouchner is workstream leader for the AMU ([Agency for the Modernisation of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agency_for_the_Modernisation_of_Ukraine "Agency for the Modernisation of Ukraine")), where he contributes his expertise in healthcare.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-2)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Kouchner was born in [Avignon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avignon "Avignon"), to a Jewish father and a Protestant mother. Kouchner's paternal grandparents were [Russian-born Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_Russia "History of the Jews in Russia") who escaped the [pogroms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pogroms "Pogroms") by immigrating to France, but perished decades later in [Auschwitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auschwitz "Auschwitz").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-3)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Kouchner began his political career as a member of the [French Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Communist_Party "French Communist Party") (PCF), from which he was expelled in 1966 for attempting to overthrow the leadership.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-4) On a visit to [Cuba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba "Cuba") in 1964, Kouchner spent the night fishing and drinking with [Fidel Castro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fidel_Castro "Fidel Castro").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-5) In the [protests of May 1968](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_1968_in_France "May 1968 in France"), he ran the medical faculty strike committee at the [Sorbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sorbonne_(building) "Sorbonne (building)").

### Co-Founder of Médecins Sans Frontières and Médecins du Monde

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Co-Founder of Médecins Sans Frontières and Médecins du Monde")]

Kouchner worked as a physician for the [Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Cross "Red Cross") in [Biafra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biafra "Biafra") in 1968 (during the [Nigerian Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigerian_Civil_War "Nigerian Civil War")). His experience as a physician for the Red Cross led him to co-found [Médecins Sans Frontières](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A9decins_Sans_Fronti%C3%A8res "Médecins Sans Frontières") (Doctors Without Borders) in 1971, and then, due to a conflict of opinion with MSF chairman [Claude Malhuret](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_Malhuret "Claude Malhuret"), he established _[Doctors of the World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A9decins\_du\_Monde "Médecins du Monde")_ ('Médecins du Monde') in 1980. Kouchner worked as a humanitarian volunteer during the Siege of Naba'a refugee camp in Lebanon in East Beirut during the [Lebanese Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanese_Civil_War "Lebanese Civil War") taking risks that "other foreign aid workers weren't, even worked closely with the [Shia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shia "Shia") cleric [Imam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imam "Imam")[Musa al-Sadr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musa_al-Sadr "Musa al-Sadr")".[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-6)

### Career in government

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Career in government")]

From 1988, Kouchner began his government career in Socialist governments, though he was not always a member of the [Socialist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_Party_(France) "Socialist Party (France)") (PS). He became "Secrétaire d'état", a lower position in the Cabinet, for Humanitarian Action in 1988 in the [Michel Rocard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michel_Rocard "Michel Rocard") cabinet, then [Minister of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_Health_(France) "Minister of Health (France)") under [Pierre Bérégovoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_B%C3%A9r%C3%A9govoy "Pierre Bérégovoy") in 1992, during [Mitterrand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitterrand "Mitterrand")'s presidency.

### Member of the European Parliament, 1994–1997

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Member of the European Parliament, 1994–1997")]

Kouchner continued his political career in the [European Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Parliament "European Parliament") from 1994 to 1997. During the time, he chaired the [Committee on Development and Cooperation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Committee_on_Development "Committee on Development") and served on the [Subcommittee on Human Rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subcommittee_on_Human_Rights "Subcommittee on Human Rights"). In addition to his committee assignments, he was a member of the Parliament's delegation for relations with the [People's Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Republic_of_China "People's Republic of China").

Together with Judge [Andrée Ruffo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9e_Ruffo "Andrée Ruffo"), Kouchner established the [International Bureau for Children's Rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Bureau_for_Children's_Rights "International Bureau for Children's Rights") (IBCR), a [non-governmental organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-governmental_organization "Non-governmental organization") based in Montreal, in 1994.

### Minister of Health, 1997–1999

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Minister of Health, 1997–1999")]

When [Lionel Jospin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Jospin "Lionel Jospin") became Prime Minister in 1997, Kouchner became [Minister of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_Health_(France) "Minister of Health (France)") for the second time. He held the office until 1999.

### UN Representative in Kosovo, 1999–2001

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: UN Representative in Kosovo, 1999–2001")]

On 15 July 1999, pursuant to [Security Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Security_Council "Security Council")[Resolution 1244](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN_Security_Council_Resolution_1244 "UN Security Council Resolution 1244"), [UN Secretary General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN_Secretary_General "UN Secretary General")[Kofi Annan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Annan "Kofi Annan") nominated Kouchner as the second [UN Special Representative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Representative_of_the_Secretary-General "Special Representative of the Secretary-General") and Head of the United Nations Interim Administration Mission in Kosovo ([UNMIK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Interim_Administration_Mission_in_Kosovo "United Nations Interim Administration Mission in Kosovo")).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-7) During 18 months, he led UN efforts to create a new civil administration and political system replacing the [Serbian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbia "Serbia") ones, and to rebuild the economy shattered by the [Kosovo War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kosovo_War "Kosovo War"). Thus, [municipal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal "Municipal") councils were elected at local level by the end of 2000.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-8) He was replaced on 21 January 2001 by [Danish Social Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_Democrats_(Denmark) "Social Democrats (Denmark)")[Hans Hækkerup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hans_H%C3%A6kkerup "Hans Hækkerup"). Later, he was awarded an honorary doctorate by the [University of Pristina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universiteti_i_Prishtin%C3%ABs "Universiteti i Prishtinës") for his services to Kosovo.

### Minister of Health, 2001–2002

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Minister of Health, 2001–2002")]

Kouchner became at this time [Minister of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_Health_(France) "Minister of Health (France)") for the third time, until the 2002 elections.

### Candidate for UN positions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Candidate for UN positions")]

In 2005, Kouchner was a candidate for the position of [United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_High_Commissioner_for_Refugees "United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees") (UNHCR), but lost the appointment in favor of former Portuguese Prime Minister, [António Guterres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant%C3%B3nio_Guterres "António Guterres"), who was nominated by then-[UN Secretary-General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Secretary-General "United Nations Secretary-General")[Kofi Annan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Annan "Kofi Annan").

In 2006, Kouchner was also a candidate to become [Director-General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Health_Organization#Directors-General_of_WHO "World Health Organization") of the [World Health Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Health_Organization "World Health Organization").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-9) He lost before the final election round, and (Hong Kong) Chinese candidate [Margaret Chan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Chan "Margaret Chan") was later elected.

In 2007, the [European Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Commission "European Commission") appointed Kouchner as its representative on the [International Independent Group of Eminent Persons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Independent_Group_of_Eminent_Persons "International Independent Group of Eminent Persons") (IIGEP), a group of individuals nominated by international donor countries and the [government of Sri Lanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Sri_Lanka "Government of Sri Lanka"), vested with a wide mandate to observe all investigations and inquiries conducted by and on behalf of the Commission of Inquiry into alleged [human rights abuses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_rights_abuses "Human rights abuses") in Sri Lanka.

### Minister of Foreign Affairs, 2007–2010

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Minister of Foreign Affairs, 2007–2010")]

After the election of [Nicolas Sarkozy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolas_Sarkozy "Nicolas Sarkozy") as [President of France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_France "President of France") in 2007, Kouchner was appointed [Minister of Foreign Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_Foreign_Affairs_(France) "Minister of Foreign Affairs (France)") in [Prime Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_France "Prime Minister of France")[François Fillon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Fillon "François Fillon")'s government, even though Kouchner supported Sarkozy's Socialist rival [Ségolène Royal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9gol%C3%A8ne_Royal "Ségolène Royal") during the campaign. He has since been expelled from the Socialist Party for his acceptance of the post.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-10)

Kouchner was dismissed in the November [2010 Fillon cabinet reshuffle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Fillon_government "Third Fillon government").

## Political positions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Political positions")]

### On the U.S.-led invasion of Iraq

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: On the U.S.-led invasion of Iraq")]

Kouchner is a longtime advocate of [humanitarian intervention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humanitarian_intervention "Humanitarian intervention").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-ft.com-11) In early 2003, he pronounced himself in favour of removing [Saddam Hussein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddam_Hussein "Saddam Hussein") as President of [Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq "Iraq"),[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-ft.com-11) arguing that interference against [dictatorship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dictatorship "Dictatorship") should be a global priority, and continued to say that now, the focus should be on the actual people themselves, and that they are the only ones who could answer _yes_ or _no_ to war.

In a 4 February 2003 editorial with [Antoine Veil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antoine_Veil "Antoine Veil") in _[Le Monde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le\_Monde "Le Monde")_, entitled "Neither War Nor Saddam", Kouchner said that he was opposed to the impending [War in Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_in_Iraq "War in Iraq"), and, as the title suggests, to the remaining in power of Saddam Hussein, the removal of whom should be accomplished via a concerted UN, preferably diplomatic, solution.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-13) He later became a fierce critic of how the occupation was subsequently conducted.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-ft.com-11)

### On Europe

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: On Europe")]

Kouchner is a well-known pro-European. He supported the ratification of the [Lisbon Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon_Treaty "Lisbon Treaty") when it was threatened to be rejected by the Irish in referendum.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-14) In the run up to the [referendum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty-eighth_Amendment_of_the_Constitution_of_Ireland "Twenty-eighth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland") in the Republic of Ireland on the ratification of the [Treaty of Lisbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Lisbon "Treaty of Lisbon"), Kouchner warned that any "No" vote towards the treaty would be detrimental to Ireland and the Irish economy. He also commented that "It would be very, very awkward if we were not able to count on the Irish, who have often counted on Europe".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-15) His comments were dismissed as "unhelpful" by leading Irish politicians, and some media commentators have suggested that his remarks may have galvanised the "No" campaign in the run up to the rejection of the Lisbon Treaty on 13 June 2008.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-16)

In 2012, Kouchner co-signed the [George Soros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Soros "George Soros") call for a strengthening of the European prerogatives as an answer to the eurozone crisis.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-17)

### Comments on Iran nuclear situation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Comments on Iran nuclear situation")]

In September 2007, Kouchner's public comments on the [Iranian nuclear situation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_program_of_Iran "Nuclear program of Iran") attracted much attention and controversy. In an interview on 16 September 2007, he said, "We will negotiate until the end. And at the same time we must prepare ourselves [...] for the worst...The worst, it's war".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-BBC-18) He stated that France was committed to a diplomatic resolution and that no military action was planned, but that an Iranian nuclear weapon would pose "a real danger for the whole world".[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-19) Iranian officials criticized the comments as "inflammatory".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-BBC-18) The chief UN nuclear inspector [Mohamed ElBaradei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohamed_ElBaradei "Mohamed ElBaradei"), the head of the [International Atomic Energy Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Atomic_Energy_Agency "International Atomic Energy Agency") indirectly responded to Kouchner by characterizing talk of attacking Iran as "hype", saying the use of force should only be considered as a last resort and only if authorized by the [UN Security Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN_Security_Council "UN Security Council").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-20)

"I would not talk about any use of force", he said. On 18 September 2007, Kouchner attempted to respond to criticisms. In comments to newspaper _[Le Monde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le\_Monde "Le Monde")_, he stated, "I do not want it to be said that I am a warmonger! [...] My message was a message of peace, of seriousness and of determination. [...] The worst situation would be war. To avoid that, the French attitude is to negotiate, negotiate, negotiate, without fear of being rebuffed, and to work with our European friends on credible sanctions."[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-21)

### Comments on a unity government for Zimbabwe

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Comments on a unity government for Zimbabwe")]

On 1 July 2008, France assumed the [presidency of the Council of the European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_the_Council_of_the_European_Union "Presidency of the Council of the European Union"). In his capacity as the French foreign minister, he commented after the [African Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Union "African Union") summit, that the European Union would only recognise a [Zimbabwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwe "Zimbabwe") unity government headed by [Morgan Tsvangirai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_Tsvangirai "Morgan Tsvangirai") not [Robert Mugabe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Mugabe "Robert Mugabe").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-22)

### Use of condoms to prevent AIDS in Africa

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Use of condoms to prevent AIDS in Africa")]

Kouchner denounced statements by [Pope Benedict XVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Benedict_XVI "Pope Benedict XVI") claiming that condoms promoted AIDS, saying they were "the opposite of tolerance and understanding".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-23)

## Life after politics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Life after politics")]

After leaving politics, Kouchner took on a variety of positions, including the following:

*   [American University of Kurdistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_American_University_of_Kurdistan "The American University of Kurdistan") (AUK), Member of the Board of Trustees[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-24)
*   [Aurora Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Prize_for_Awakening_Humanity "Aurora Prize for Awakening Humanity"), Member of the Selection Committee (since 2017)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-25)
*   _[Devex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devex "Devex")_, Member of the Board of Advisors[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-26)
*   Echo Foundation, Member of the International Board of Advisors[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-27)
*   [European Council on Foreign Relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Council_on_Foreign_Relations "European Council on Foreign Relations") (ECFR), Member[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-28)
*   [Fondation Agir Contre l'Exclusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fondation_Agir_Contre_l'Exclusion "Fondation Agir Contre l'Exclusion") (FACE), Member of the Board
*   [International Campaign for Tibet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Campaign_for_Tibet "International Campaign for Tibet") (ICT), Member of the International Council of Advisors[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-29)
*   Toledo International Centre for Peace (CITpax), Member of the Advisory Council[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-30)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Kouchner has three children (Julien, [Camille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camille_Kouchner "Camille Kouchner") and Antoine) by his first wife, [Évelyne Pisier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89velyne_Pisier "Évelyne Pisier"), a law professor, and one child, Alexandre, by his present wife [Christine Ockrent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christine_Ockrent "Christine Ockrent"), a TV anchor and author.

**Bernard Kouchner** (born 1 November 1939) is a French politician and doctor. He is the co-founder of [Médecins Sans Frontières](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A9decins_Sans_Fronti%C3%A8res "Médecins Sans Frontières") (MSF) and [Médecins du Monde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A9decins_du_Monde "Médecins du Monde"). From 2007 until 2010, he was the French [Minister of Foreign and European Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_Foreign_Affairs_(France) "Minister of Foreign Affairs (France)") in the center-right [Fillon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Fillon "François Fillon") government under president [Nicolas Sarkozy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolas_Sarkozy "Nicolas Sarkozy"), although he had been in the past a minister in socialist governments and was himself a long-term member of the [Socialist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_Party_(France) "Socialist Party (France)"). 2010, _[The Jerusalem Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Jerusalem\_Post "The Jerusalem Post")_ considered Kouchner the 15th most influential Jew in the world.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-1) Since 2015 Kouchner is workstream leader for the AMU ([Agency for the Modernisation of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agency_for_the_Modernisation_of_Ukraine "Agency for the Modernisation of Ukraine")), where he contributes his expertise in healthcare.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-2)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Kouchner was born in [Avignon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avignon "Avignon"), to a Jewish father and a Protestant mother. Kouchner's paternal grandparents were [Russian-born Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_Russia "History of the Jews in Russia") who escaped the [pogroms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pogroms "Pogroms") by immigrating to France, but perished decades later in [Auschwitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auschwitz "Auschwitz").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-3)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Kouchner began his political career as a member of the [French Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Communist_Party "French Communist Party") (PCF), from which he was expelled in 1966 for attempting to overthrow the leadership.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-4) On a visit to [Cuba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba "Cuba") in 1964, Kouchner spent the night fishing and drinking with [Fidel Castro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fidel_Castro "Fidel Castro").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-5) In the [protests of May 1968](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_1968_in_France "May 1968 in France"), he ran the medical faculty strike committee at the [Sorbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sorbonne_(building) "Sorbonne (building)").

### Co-Founder of Médecins Sans Frontières and Médecins du Monde

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Co-Founder of Médecins Sans Frontières and Médecins du Monde")]

Kouchner worked as a physician for the [Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Cross "Red Cross") in [Biafra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biafra "Biafra") in 1968 (during the [Nigerian Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigerian_Civil_War "Nigerian Civil War")). His experience as a physician for the Red Cross led him to co-found [Médecins Sans Frontières](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A9decins_Sans_Fronti%C3%A8res "Médecins Sans Frontières") (Doctors Without Borders) in 1971, and then, due to a conflict of opinion with MSF chairman [Claude Malhuret](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_Malhuret "Claude Malhuret"), he established _[Doctors of the World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A9decins\_du\_Monde "Médecins du Monde")_ ('Médecins du Monde') in 1980. Kouchner worked as a humanitarian volunteer during the Siege of Naba'a refugee camp in Lebanon in East Beirut during the [Lebanese Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanese_Civil_War "Lebanese Civil War") taking risks that "other foreign aid workers weren't, even worked closely with the [Shia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shia "Shia") cleric [Imam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imam "Imam")[Musa al-Sadr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musa_al-Sadr "Musa al-Sadr")".[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-6)

### Career in government

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Career in government")]

From 1988, Kouchner began his government career in Socialist governments, though he was not always a member of the [Socialist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_Party_(France) "Socialist Party (France)") (PS). He became "Secrétaire d'état", a lower position in the Cabinet, for Humanitarian Action in 1988 in the [Michel Rocard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michel_Rocard "Michel Rocard") cabinet, then [Minister of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_Health_(France) "Minister of Health (France)") under [Pierre Bérégovoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_B%C3%A9r%C3%A9govoy "Pierre Bérégovoy") in 1992, during [Mitterrand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitterrand "Mitterrand")'s presidency.

### Member of the European Parliament, 1994–1997

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Member of the European Parliament, 1994–1997")]

Kouchner continued his political career in the [European Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Parliament "European Parliament") from 1994 to 1997. During the time, he chaired the [Committee on Development and Cooperation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Committee_on_Development "Committee on Development") and served on the [Subcommittee on Human Rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subcommittee_on_Human_Rights "Subcommittee on Human Rights"). In addition to his committee assignments, he was a member of the Parliament's delegation for relations with the [People's Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Republic_of_China "People's Republic of China").

Together with Judge [Andrée Ruffo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9e_Ruffo "Andrée Ruffo"), Kouchner established the [International Bureau for Children's Rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Bureau_for_Children's_Rights "International Bureau for Children's Rights") (IBCR), a [non-governmental organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-governmental_organization "Non-governmental organization") based in Montreal, in 1994.

### Minister of Health, 1997–1999

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Minister of Health, 1997–1999")]

When [Lionel Jospin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Jospin "Lionel Jospin") became Prime Minister in 1997, Kouchner became [Minister of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_Health_(France) "Minister of Health (France)") for the second time. He held the office until 1999.

### UN Representative in Kosovo, 1999–2001

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: UN Representative in Kosovo, 1999–2001")]

On 15 July 1999, pursuant to [Security Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Security_Council "Security Council")[Resolution 1244](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN_Security_Council_Resolution_1244 "UN Security Council Resolution 1244"), [UN Secretary General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN_Secretary_General "UN Secretary General")[Kofi Annan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Annan "Kofi Annan") nominated Kouchner as the second [UN Special Representative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Representative_of_the_Secretary-General "Special Representative of the Secretary-General") and Head of the United Nations Interim Administration Mission in Kosovo ([UNMIK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Interim_Administration_Mission_in_Kosovo "United Nations Interim Administration Mission in Kosovo")).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-7) During 18 months, he led UN efforts to create a new civil administration and political system replacing the [Serbian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbia "Serbia") ones, and to rebuild the economy shattered by the [Kosovo War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kosovo_War "Kosovo War"). Thus, [municipal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal "Municipal") councils were elected at local level by the end of 2000.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-8) He was replaced on 21 January 2001 by [Danish Social Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_Democrats_(Denmark) "Social Democrats (Denmark)")[Hans Hækkerup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hans_H%C3%A6kkerup "Hans Hækkerup"). Later, he was awarded an honorary doctorate by the [University of Pristina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universiteti_i_Prishtin%C3%ABs "Universiteti i Prishtinës") for his services to Kosovo.

### Minister of Health, 2001–2002

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Minister of Health, 2001–2002")]

Kouchner became at this time [Minister of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_Health_(France) "Minister of Health (France)") for the third time, until the 2002 elections.

### Candidate for UN positions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Candidate for UN positions")]

In 2005, Kouchner was a candidate for the position of [United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_High_Commissioner_for_Refugees "United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees") (UNHCR), but lost the appointment in favor of former Portuguese Prime Minister, [António Guterres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant%C3%B3nio_Guterres "António Guterres"), who was nominated by then-[UN Secretary-General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Secretary-General "United Nations Secretary-General")[Kofi Annan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Annan "Kofi Annan").

In 2006, Kouchner was also a candidate to become [Director-General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Health_Organization#Directors-General_of_WHO "World Health Organization") of the [World Health Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Health_Organization "World Health Organization").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-9) He lost before the final election round, and (Hong Kong) Chinese candidate [Margaret Chan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Chan "Margaret Chan") was later elected.

In 2007, the [European Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Commission "European Commission") appointed Kouchner as its representative on the [International Independent Group of Eminent Persons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Independent_Group_of_Eminent_Persons "International Independent Group of Eminent Persons") (IIGEP), a group of individuals nominated by international donor countries and the [government of Sri Lanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Sri_Lanka "Government of Sri Lanka"), vested with a wide mandate to observe all investigations and inquiries conducted by and on behalf of the Commission of Inquiry into alleged [human rights abuses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_rights_abuses "Human rights abuses") in Sri Lanka.

### Minister of Foreign Affairs, 2007–2010

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Minister of Foreign Affairs, 2007–2010")]

After the election of [Nicolas Sarkozy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolas_Sarkozy "Nicolas Sarkozy") as [President of France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_France "President of France") in 2007, Kouchner was appointed [Minister of Foreign Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_Foreign_Affairs_(France) "Minister of Foreign Affairs (France)") in [Prime Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_France "Prime Minister of France")[François Fillon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Fillon "François Fillon")'s government, even though Kouchner supported Sarkozy's Socialist rival [Ségolène Royal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9gol%C3%A8ne_Royal "Ségolène Royal") during the campaign. He has since been expelled from the Socialist Party for his acceptance of the post.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-10)

Kouchner was dismissed in the November [2010 Fillon cabinet reshuffle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Fillon_government "Third Fillon government").

## Political positions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Political positions")]

### On the U.S.-led invasion of Iraq

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: On the U.S.-led invasion of Iraq")]

Kouchner is a longtime advocate of [humanitarian intervention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humanitarian_intervention "Humanitarian intervention").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-ft.com-11) In early 2003, he pronounced himself in favour of removing [Saddam Hussein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddam_Hussein "Saddam Hussein") as President of [Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq "Iraq"),[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-ft.com-11) arguing that interference against [dictatorship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dictatorship "Dictatorship") should be a global priority, and continued to say that now, the focus should be on the actual people themselves, and that they are the only ones who could answer _yes_ or _no_ to war.

In a 4 February 2003 editorial with [Antoine Veil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antoine_Veil "Antoine Veil") in _[Le Monde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le\_Monde "Le Monde")_, entitled "Neither War Nor Saddam", Kouchner said that he was opposed to the impending [War in Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_in_Iraq "War in Iraq"), and, as the title suggests, to the remaining in power of Saddam Hussein, the removal of whom should be accomplished via a concerted UN, preferably diplomatic, solution.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-13) He later became a fierce critic of how the occupation was subsequently conducted.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-ft.com-11)

### On Europe

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: On Europe")]

Kouchner is a well-known pro-European. He supported the ratification of the [Lisbon Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon_Treaty "Lisbon Treaty") when it was threatened to be rejected by the Irish in referendum.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-14) In the run up to the [referendum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty-eighth_Amendment_of_the_Constitution_of_Ireland "Twenty-eighth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland") in the Republic of Ireland on the ratification of the [Treaty of Lisbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Lisbon "Treaty of Lisbon"), Kouchner warned that any "No" vote towards the treaty would be detrimental to Ireland and the Irish economy. He also commented that "It would be very, very awkward if we were not able to count on the Irish, who have often counted on Europe".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-15) His comments were dismissed as "unhelpful" by leading Irish politicians, and some media commentators have suggested that his remarks may have galvanised the "No" campaign in the run up to the rejection of the Lisbon Treaty on 13 June 2008.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-16)

In 2012, Kouchner co-signed the [George Soros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Soros "George Soros") call for a strengthening of the European prerogatives as an answer to the eurozone crisis.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-17)

### Comments on Iran nuclear situation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Comments on Iran nuclear situation")]

In September 2007, Kouchner's public comments on the [Iranian nuclear situation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_program_of_Iran "Nuclear program of Iran") attracted much attention and controversy. In an interview on 16 September 2007, he said, "We will negotiate until the end. And at the same time we must prepare ourselves [...] for the worst...The worst, it's war".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-BBC-18) He stated that France was committed to a diplomatic resolution and that no military action was planned, but that an Iranian nuclear weapon would pose "a real danger for the whole world".[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-19) Iranian officials criticized the comments as "inflammatory".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-BBC-18) The chief UN nuclear inspector [Mohamed ElBaradei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohamed_ElBaradei "Mohamed ElBaradei"), the head of the [International Atomic Energy Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Atomic_Energy_Agency "International Atomic Energy Agency") indirectly responded to Kouchner by characterizing talk of attacking Iran as "hype", saying the use of force should only be considered as a last resort and only if authorized by the [UN Security Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN_Security_Council "UN Security Council").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-20)

"I would not talk about any use of force", he said. On 18 September 2007, Kouchner attempted to respond to criticisms. In comments to newspaper _[Le Monde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le\_Monde "Le Monde")_, he stated, "I do not want it to be said that I am a warmonger! [...] My message was a message of peace, of seriousness and of determination. [...] The worst situation would be war. To avoid that, the French attitude is to negotiate, negotiate, negotiate, without fear of being rebuffed, and to work with our European friends on credible sanctions."[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-21)

### Comments on a unity government for Zimbabwe

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Comments on a unity government for Zimbabwe")]

On 1 July 2008, France assumed the [presidency of the Council of the European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_the_Council_of_the_European_Union "Presidency of the Council of the European Union"). In his capacity as the French foreign minister, he commented after the [African Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Union "African Union") summit, that the European Union would only recognise a [Zimbabwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwe "Zimbabwe") unity government headed by [Morgan Tsvangirai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_Tsvangirai "Morgan Tsvangirai") not [Robert Mugabe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Mugabe "Robert Mugabe").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-22)

### Use of condoms to prevent AIDS in Africa

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Use of condoms to prevent AIDS in Africa")]

Kouchner denounced statements by [Pope Benedict XVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Benedict_XVI "Pope Benedict XVI") claiming that condoms promoted AIDS, saying they were "the opposite of tolerance and understanding".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-23)

## Life after politics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Life after politics")]

After leaving politics, Kouchner took on a variety of positions, including the following:

*   [American University of Kurdistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_American_University_of_Kurdistan "The American University of Kurdistan") (AUK), Member of the Board of Trustees[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-24)
*   [Aurora Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Prize_for_Awakening_Humanity "Aurora Prize for Awakening Humanity"), Member of the Selection Committee (since 2017)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-25)
*   _[Devex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devex "Devex")_, Member of the Board of Advisors[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-26)
*   Echo Foundation, Member of the International Board of Advisors[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-27)
*   [European Council on Foreign Relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Council_on_Foreign_Relations "European Council on Foreign Relations") (ECFR), Member[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-28)
*   [Fondation Agir Contre l'Exclusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fondation_Agir_Contre_l'Exclusion "Fondation Agir Contre l'Exclusion") (FACE), Member of the Board
*   [International Campaign for Tibet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Campaign_for_Tibet "International Campaign for Tibet") (ICT), Member of the International Council of Advisors[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-29)
*   Toledo International Centre for Peace (CITpax), Member of the Advisory Council[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Kouchner#cite_note-30)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernard_Kouchner&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Kouchner has three children (Julien, [Camille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camille_Kouchner "Camille Kouchner") and Antoine) by his first wife, [Évelyne Pisier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89velyne_Pisier "Évelyne Pisier"), a law professor, and one child, Alexandre, by his present wife [Christine Ockrent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christine_Ockrent "Christine Ockrent"), a TV anchor and author.
